description: Machine learning and AI methods for risk modeling, tail-risk estimation, stress testing, anomaly detection, and dynamic hedging.

techniques.name: Deep Hedging
techniques.description: Framework for hedging derivatives portfolios using deep reinforcement learning, handling market frictions like transaction costs and liquidity constraints. Proposed by Buehler, Gonon, Teichmann, and Wood (2019).
techniques.verification_notes: Confirmed published in Quantitative Finance 2019. Seminal paper in the field. 15-30% hedging cost reduction vs delta hedging is consistent with literature.

techniques.name: Neural Network Value-at-Risk (VaR)
techniques.description: LSTM/GRU-based VaR models that capture time-varying volatility clustering, improving backtesting violation rates 15-25% over traditional GARCH models.
techniques.verification_notes: Neural VaR is well-documented in literature. Specific improvement percentages vary by study and market conditions.

techniques.name: GAN-Based Stress Testing
techniques.description: Generative adversarial networks that create synthetic extreme market scenarios more realistic than historical simulation, useful for regulatory stress testing.
techniques.verification_notes: Active research area. GANs for financial scenario generation confirmed in multiple papers.

techniques.name: Isolation Forests / VAE Anomaly Detection
techniques.description: Unsupervised anomaly detection for identifying market anomalies, potential flash crashes, and unusual trading patterns. Isolation forests and variational autoencoders are primary approaches.
techniques.verification_notes: Well-established techniques. 85-92% precision claim needs context - varies significantly by application and definition of anomaly.

techniques.name: Bayesian Neural Networks for Uncertainty Quantification
techniques.description: Neural networks with Bayesian inference over weights providing epistemic uncertainty estimates for risk models, important for regulatory compliance.
techniques.verification_notes: Bayesian deep learning for finance is documented. Regulatory acceptance is still developing.
